flags-answered.removed-element: overflow: The screen matched the word 'overflow' (its removed-element pattern aims at CALL ... ON OVERFLOW, §2002:G.1 item 4). Here the word is 'the page overflow condition' of a LINAGE file, an element present in both editions (§2002:13.16.32.3 GR1 = §2023:13.18.34.4 GR1, same words), not CALL ON OVERFLOW; no obsolete or archaic element is named. The reader's row had no 2002 evidence, so I ran it: pb523_linage_margins_on_the_medium_85 (logical page = sum of the phrases, zero margins) matches its .out at --std 2002 in fixed format, and probe linage_nofoot (LINAGE 3, no FOOTING) at --std 2002 raises END-OF-PAGE only at the overflowing third WRITE, not when line 3 is reached (E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out-answer/probes-a-23/linage_nofoot.cob (output linage_nofoot.2002.txt) and E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/op-20261114/read-2002/out-answer/probes-a-23/suite.2002.log).

cases.reason: The answerer enumerated 2002 class national as 'national, national-edited, numeric-edited usage national, national group items' and said the 2002 table equals 2023's; but 2002's national category (§2002:8.5.2.7 item 3) also lists 'An elementary data item explicitly or implicitly described as usage national', which 2023 §2023:8.5.2.10 (and 2014) dropped. Read literally, PIC 9(n) USAGE NATIONAL and PIC 1(n) USAGE NATIONAL are category, hence class, national in 2002, a datum the 2023 evidence never shows. Other 2002 text (§2002:13.16.22.3 GR4 'class numeric with usage national', §2002:14.8.23.3 GR2a) contradicts that reading, so it is not decisive either way; the flag answer did not address it. For THIS rule: under the literal reading a RECORD KEY PIC 9(3) USAGE NATIONAL is category national, so §2002:12.3.4.12.2 SR2 admits it and this rule then governs it as a record key of class national. The compiler refuses such a key at 2002 (COBOL0863 'category-numeric item'), so the 2023 evidence never shows this rule applied to it. Settle with one ruling (a docs/conformance entry or kb/Work decision): whether §2002:8.5.2.7 item 3, absent from 2014 and 2023, is inoperative for an elementary item whose PICTURE gives category numeric, numeric-edited or boolean (as §2002:13.16.22.3 GR4, §2002:14.8.23.3 GR2a and Table 3 presuppose), or makes such an item (also) category and class national at --std 2002. If inoperative: UPHELD. If operative: DIFFERENT, compiler-at-2002 wrong.

cases.reason: Words, format and FD reach identical, but the 2023 CONFORMS verdict for GR4 (inventory GR-13.18.10.4-4 and DRV-GR-13.18.10.4-4) rests explicitly on §2023:A.3 item 5, which lets BLOCK CONTAINS have no effect: 'Exact vs min/max physical record size has no runtime effect under the documented inert claim (A.3 item 5)'. The compiler ignores integer-1/integer-2 entirely. 2002's processor-dependent list (B.3, items 1-31) has no BLOCK CONTAINS item, and the only other BLOCK CONTAINS text in 2002 is the EXTERNAL agreement rule 13.3.4.3 GR2a. So at 2002 the requirement 'integer-2 represents the exact size of the physical record' carries no inertness excuse: 2023 conformance (via an excuse 2023 added) does not imply 2002 conformance. Needs its own 2002 verdict: either a recorded decision that 2002 permits an inert clause (the 9.1.1 'hardware dependent' sentence is the only candidate and is in 2023 too, so it was not what the 2023 verdict relied on), or the clause modeled.
